sections.title: The Last Supper and the Institution of the Lord's Supper
observations: In this section, Jesus shares the Passover meal with His disciples, which is significant as it marks the transition from the old covenant to the new covenant.
Jesus takes the bread and wine, symbolizing His body and blood, and establishes the practice of communion for His followers.
This moment emphasizes the sacrificial nature of Jesus' mission and the importance of remembrance in the Christian faith.

sections.title: Jesus Predicts Peter's Denial
observations: Jesus foretells Peter's denial, highlighting the frailty of human commitment in the face of trial.
Peter's bold declaration of loyalty contrasts with Jesus' prediction, illustrating the theme of humility and reliance on God's strength rather than our own.
This serves as a reminder that even the most devoted can falter, and it calls for self-examination and dependence on God's grace.

sections.title: Jesus in the Garden of Gethsemane
observations: In the garden, Jesus experiences deep anguish as He prays, demonstrating His humanity and the weight of the impending crucifixion.
The disciples' inability to stay awake and pray reflects the struggle of spiritual vigilance and the need for prayer in times of trial.
Jesus' submission to the Father's will is a profound example of obedience and surrender, even in the face of suffering.

sections.title: Jesus' Arrest
observations: The betrayal by Judas and the subsequent arrest of Jesus fulfill the prophecies concerning the Messiah's suffering.
Peter's impulsive reaction to defend Jesus with a sword contrasts with Jesus' message of peace and submission to God's plan.
This section highlights the theme of betrayal and the fulfillment of God's redemptive plan through the events leading to the crucifixion.

sections.title: Jesus Before the Council
observations: Jesus' trial before the religious leaders showcases the injustice and false accusations He faced.
His calm demeanor in the face of hostility exemplifies His commitment to His mission and the truth of His identity as the Son of God.
This moment serves as a reminder of the cost of discipleship and the call to stand firm in faith amidst opposition.

importantVerses.commentary: Jesus institutes the Lord's Supper, emphasizing the significance of His sacrifice and the new covenant.
Jesus reassures Peter that He has prayed for him, highlighting the importance of intercession and God's sustaining grace.
Jesus' prayer in Gethsemane reveals His struggle and ultimate submission to the Father's will, a model for our own prayers in times of distress.

questions: What does the institution of the Lord's Supper teach us about the significance of Jesus' sacrifice?
How can we apply the lessons from Peter's denial to our own lives and faith journeys?
What does Jesus' prayer in Gethsemane reveal about the nature of His mission and our own struggles with obedience?
In what ways does the account of Jesus' arrest challenge our understanding of power and submission?
How can we find strength in the face of opposition, as demonstrated by Jesus during His trial?
